newsitem.title: USA: Bus pulled out of Boston river, driver dead.
newsitem.headline: Bus pulled out of Boston river, driver dead.

text.p: Emergency crews recovered a passenger bus on Tuesday almost 12 hours after it plunged into the murky, icy Charles River, killing the driver.

The 45-year-old driver, who had worked for the Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority (MBTA) for 10 years, was found near his seat by divers about 45 minutes after the bus careened across a roadway and plunged into the river that separates Cambridge and Boston.
The $236,000 bus was head-first in the muddy bottom with just the top of its rear section poking through the surface. A huge crane was used to hoist the bus out of the water.
Once ashore, the bus's clearly illuminated out of service sign could be seen. There were no passengers on the bus.
An MBTA spokeswoman told reporters at the scene of the crash that the driver had finished his run and had been heading back to a bus yard on the other side of town.
